steps.name: Put a tour button on your page
steps.description: The bridge is a small remote control script that lets your page ask an installed Manuscript extension to replay a saved tour. Your visitors need the extension, but they get instant playback of your demo.

annotations.text: The bridge is a small remote control script that lets your page ask an installed Manuscript extension to replay a saved tour. Your visitors need the extension, but they get instant playback of your demo.

steps.name: Option A — your own button
steps.description: Author the button yourself with your own styling. When the extension is missing, send visitors to the Web Store or your own homepage via openStore() and openHomepage() API calls.

annotations.text: Author the button yourself with your own styling. When the extension is missing, send visitors to the Web Store or your own homepage via openStore() and openHomepage() API calls.

steps.name: Option B — let the bridge mount
steps.description: Zero-DOM-touch approach. The bridge mounts a Shadow-DOM-isolated launcher pill to your page's bottom-right. It shows "Take the tour" when the extension is installed, or "Install Manuscript" when it's missing.

annotations.text: Zero-DOM-touch approach. The bridge mounts a Shadow-DOM-isolated launcher pill to your page's bottom-right. It shows "Take the tour" when the extension is installed, or "Install Manuscript" when it's missing.

steps.name: Public API — full control
steps.description: The manuscript.* API gives you full control: isInstalled(), load(), play(), pause(), next(), prev(), jump(), exit(), plus openStore() and openHomepage() for extension prompts.

annotations.text: The manuscript.* API gives you full control: isInstalled(), load(), play(), pause(), next(), prev(), jump(), exit(), plus openStore() and openHomepage() for extension prompts.

steps.name: Downloads and getting started
steps.description: Download the bridge library (14 KB, dependency-free) and example tour JSON. The library plugs into your page, and you author tours with the Manuscript extension then export them as JSON.

annotations.text: Download the bridge library (14 KB, dependency-free) and example tour JSON. The library plugs into your page, and you author tours with the Manuscript extension then export them as JSON.
